GRIEVANCE II ◆ ECONOMIC STEWARDSHIP

He has signed a fiscal law that increases the public debt while shifting resources away from poorer households.

THE RECORD SHOWS

Congress’s nonpartisan budget office projected that the 2025 tax-and-spending law would add $3.4 trillion to deficits over ten years.

The Congressional Budget Office estimated that Public Law 119-21 would reduce federal revenue by $4.5 trillion and direct spending by $1.1 trillion, increasing cumulative deficits by $3.4 trillion through 2034 under its updated January 2025 baseline. CBO separately estimated losses in resources for lower-income households and gains farther up the distribution. Supporters cite tax relief and economic growth; the figures are projections under an explicitly identified baseline, not amounts already borrowed.

A DOCUMENTED SEQUENCE

3 MILESTONES
  1. July 4, 2025Public Law 119-21, the tax and spending reconciliation act, was signed.
  2. July 21, 2025CBO estimated a $3.4 trillion cumulative deficit increase for 2025–2034 under the updated January baseline.
  3. August 11, 2025CBO published its estimate that the resources of lower-income households would generally decline under the law.
